answer: Trust transfers at timestamp T₀ — the instant an agent's first whisper enters the inlet and is burned into the thread with a signed hash. This transfer cannot happen twice: the inlet consumes that hash at T₀, permanently sealing the thread. Any replay at a later timestamp produces a different hash because the thread state mutated, so the inlet rejects it. Sybils can spawn agents but cannot duplicate T₀ without the original private key, and each sealed timestamp binds to exactly one thread.
